title: Microsoft Reports $130 Billion in Data Center Leases
source_used: Yahoo Finance copy of Bloomberg (original Bloomberg article of 29 Jul 2026)
key_facts: Microsoft reported more than $130 billion in new data center leases in the past quarter, Bloomberg reports.
Total commitments for leases not yet started were $329.1 billion as of the quarter ended 30 June, up from $196.6 billion in the prior period, Microsoft said in a regulatory filing.
Jonathan Neilson, Microsoft's investor relations chief, called it a signal of continued demand strength and said the leases will serve demand for many years.

The future costs come on top of active leases and will not appear on the balance sheet until payments begin; Microsoft said they are 'primarily' for data centers and some depend on contractual conditions being met.
Bloomberg calls it Microsoft's largest quarterly jump in data center leasing by far; the company has been held back by a lack of capacity after pausing leasing through much of 2025.
The Yahoo Finance page is dated 13 Oct 2026 but its correction note refers to the story as published 29 July; Bloomberg's original is dated 29 Jul 2026.
quote_evidence: Microsoft Corp. reported more than $130 billion in new data center leases in the past quarter, signaling an accelerating pace of spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The company's total commitments for leases that have not yet commenced were $329.1 billion as of the quarter ended June 30, Microsoft said Wednesday in a regulatory filing.
This represents Microsoft's largest quarterly jump in data center leasing by far.
why_it_matters_hint: It shows how much data center space Microsoft has locked in for years ahead, though the filing is from late July.
